390.answer:
Here's what your notebook contains on the PLTR trade [1]:

Entry: Planned entry at 26.35 through the handle high, based on a nine-week cup with handle pattern (handle low at 24.10) [1].

Stop: 24.85, which keeps risk under six percent [1]. You also noted a separate invalidation rule: if the breakout fails back under 25.40 on volume, you'll exit the whole position that same day rather than wait for the stop [1].

Risks:
- Government budget timing — the Army contract renewal slips into the next fiscal year [1].
- Stock-based compensation, still running near 20 percent of revenue, diluting holders every quarter [1].
- Valuation risk generally — you noted the valuation "leaves little room for a miss," which is why you're sizing the position at half of normal [1].
- Market risk — if the broader market rolls over, you'll skip the trade entirely, since "breakouts fail in corrections no matter how clean the chart" [1].

Final rule for the trade: No adds until the stock closes above 28 for two days in a row [1].

Additional context you recorded: first target is 31 (the measured move from the cup), where you'd trim a third [1]; earnings are five weeks out; and the lesson from a prior attempt was buying the first pop and giving back the gain within three sessions [1].
